records.name: Burns Cottage
records.description: Burns Cottage is the birthplace of Robert Burns, Scotland's national poet, who was born at the cottage on 25 January 1759. It is located in Alloway, a current suburb of Ayr, and a former village, located in South Ayrshire, Scotland. The cottage was built by Robert Burns' father, William Burnes in 1757 and is a four-roomed clay and thatch cottage which has been fully restored to become part of the Robert Burns Birthplace Museum.

records.name: Robert Burns Birthplace Museum
records.description: The Robert Burns Birthplace Museum is a museum which houses collections relating to the life of Robert Burns, Scotland's national Bard. It is run by the National Trust for Scotland (NTS) and is located within Alloway in Ayrshire, the village where Burns was born. It neighbours Burn's Cottage, the house in which Burns was born.

records.name: Burns Monument and Gardens
records.description: Landscaped memorial gardens and dramatic 19th-century monument celebrating Robert Burns beside the Brig o' Doon and museum complex.
records.hours: Open daily (gardens open all hours; monument Apr–Oct 10am–5pm)

records.name: Brig o' Doon
records.description: The Brig o' Doon, sometimes called the Auld Brig or Old Bridge of Doon, is a late medieval bridge over the River Doon in Ayrshire, Scotland, and a Category A listed historic structure.
records.address: Brig o' Doon, Alloway, Ayr KA7 4PQ

records.name: Auld Kirk, Alloway
records.description: Atmospheric ruined medieval kirk made famous in Tam o' Shanter, standing among old gravestones in the heart of Burns Country.

records.name: Poet's Path
records.description: Short landscaped path linking the museum, Brig o' Doon and Burns Monument through the heart of Burns Country.

records.name: Greenan Castle
records.description: Greenan Castle is a 16th-century ruined tower house, around 2+1⁄2 miles southwest of Ayr in South Ayrshire, Scotland. Situated at the top of a sea cliff, it was originally a promontory fort converted into a motte-and-bailey in the 12th century. In the 15th century a tower house was built by the Lords of the Isles, which later passed into the hands of the Kennedy family.

records.name: Doonfoot Beach
records.description: Quiet stretch of sand near Alloway at the mouth of the River Doon, ideal for coastal walks and views back to Greenan Castle.

records.name: River Doon Walk
records.description: Scenic riverside walks around Alloway following the waterway made famous in Burns's poetry.

records.name: Souter Johnnie's Cottage
records.description: Traditional thatched cottage in Kirkoswald associated with Burns's Tam o' Shanter and its convivial cobbler character.

records.name: Shanter Farm
records.description: Farm setting tied to the Tam o' Shanter story and often associated with wider Burns Country visits.

records.name: Land o' Burns Visitor Centre
records.description: Burns-themed visitor stop interpreting the poet's life, characters and the surrounding countryside.

records.name: Alloway Village
records.description: Picturesque village core where many of Burns Country's best-known landmarks sit within walking distance.

records.name: Burns Monument Lookout
records.description: Pleasant viewpoint around the monument gardens with leafy views toward the Doon valley.

records.name: Cambusdoon House
records.description: Historic estate site near Alloway associated with the broader landscape of Burns Country and old Ayrshire families.

records.name: Alloway Tunnel Greenway
records.description: Leafy path using the line of an old railway corridor on the edge of Burns Country.

records.name: Tam o' Shanter Trail
records.description: Themed route linking Alloway's kirk, bridge, monument and museum through the landscapes that inspired Burns.

records.name: Burns Memorial Gardens Walk
records.description: Short landscaped walk around the Burns Monument grounds, especially attractive in spring and summer.

records.name: Croy Shore
records.description: Rocky and sandy shore south of Ayr, known for open sea views and access toward Electric Brae and Dunure.

records.name: Kennedy's Pass
records.description: Dramatic coastal viewpoint in the Carrick area, pairing clifftop scenery with a sense of old routeways.

records.name: Culzean Castle
records.description: One of Scotland's greatest clifftop castles and a natural extension of an Alloway or Burns Country itinerary.

records.name: Culzean Country Park
records.description: Extensive coastal estate with gardens, woodland, beaches and sea views in the wider Burns Country region.

records.name: Culzean Beach
records.description: Beach below the Culzean estate with cliffs, caves and broad Firth of Clyde views.

records.name: Crossraguel Abbey
records.description: Magnificent red-stone abbey ruin near Maybole, one of the richest medieval sites in south-west Scotland.

records.name: Maybole Castle
records.description: Tall urban castle on the High Street of old Carrick's capital, often paired with Burns Country touring.

records.name: Bachelors' Club
records.description: National Trust for Scotland site in Tarbolton where Burns and friends once met, deepening the poet's local story.

records.name: Kirkoswald Village
records.description: Attractive village associated with Burns characters, old coaching routes and nearby literary landmarks.

records.name: Kirkoswald Old Kirk
records.description: Ruined kirk and kirkyard adding atmosphere to a Burns-themed detour toward the coast.

records.name: Turnberry Lighthouse
records.description: Classic Carrick lighthouse and golfing landmark visible on longer Burns Country coastal drives.

records.name: Ailsa Craig Viewpoint
records.description: Fine viewpoint toward Ailsa Craig, the volcanic island that dominates many South Ayrshire seascapes.

records.name: Heads of Ayr Farm Park
records.description: Family-friendly coastal attraction just south of Ayr and easy to combine with Alloway village sights.

records.name: Belleisle House
records.description: Historic house in the parkland south of Ayr, close enough to feature on wider Alloway itineraries.

records.name: Rozelle House Galleries
records.description: Art venue and cultural stop in Rozelle Park, just north of Alloway.

records.name: Maidens Harbour
records.description: Pretty little harbour village on the Carrick coast, good for views and short shoreline walks.

records.name: Dunure Harbour
records.description: Characterful small harbour below Dunure Castle, combining boats, cliffs and the Ayrshire Coastal Path.

records.name: Carrick Hills Viewpoint
records.description: Upland viewpoint in the old Carrick district with sweeping rural panoramas back toward the coast.

records.name: Greenan Shore
records.description: Shoreline walk below Greenan Castle with rocky coves and classic views north to Ayr and south to Alloway.

records.name: Low Green
records.description: Broad seafront lawn in Ayr that forms part of many longer Burns Country beach and town walks.

records.name: Burns Monument Centre
records.description: Striking restored church venue in Ayr, adding another Burns-associated stop near Alloway.

records.name: Heads of Ayr Beach
records.description: Open coastal stretch south of Ayr with views toward the Carrick shore and Arran.
